reason: The crane needs a stable frame, so I'll start by mounting the mast on the base.
expectation: I expect an upright frame that can later be braced against sideways bending.

alternatives.reason: The pulley will likely be useful for lifting, but the frame comes first.

effect: The upright mast is in place, so it can now be braced.
reaction: A straightforward start; nothing surprising yet.
reason: Diagonal braces should help the mast resist bending sideways, directly addressing the goal.
expectation: I expect a more rigid mast frame, with the braces preventing it from leaning sideways.

alternatives.reason: The pulley will be useful later, but bracing the mast addresses the current goal.

effect: The triangular braces explain how the mast resists sideways distortion; next I can prepare the boom.
reaction: The rectangle-to-diamond comparison makes the bracing easy to understand.
reason: I'll prepare the boom so it can eventually pivot on the crane frame.
expectation: I expect a boom with a hinge pin ready to attach to the mast.

alternatives.reason: The pulley also needs assembling, but I chose to prepare the boom first.

effect: The boom now has its hinge pin and is ready to attach to the braced mast.
reason: Attaching the boom advances the crane frame.
expectation: I expect the boom to pivot on the mast, possibly needing further support.

alternatives.reason: The pulley also needs assembly, but I'll attach the boom first.

effect: The boom is attached to the braced mast; it can now receive its support stay.
reason: The stay should support the hinged boom and make the frame more stable.
expectation: I expect the boom to be held in position rather than swinging freely.

alternatives.reason: The pulley needs assembly too, but supporting the boom seems more immediate.

effect: The stay now holds the boom; assembling the pulley is the only offered combination.
reaction: The boom support was a straightforward step.
reason: I'll assemble the pulley, the only available combination.
expectation: I expect a pulley assembly that can be fitted to the crane.

effect: The assembled pulley will redirect the pull without reducing the load; it is ready to fit to the boom.
reaction: The distinction between changing direction and reducing weight is useful.
reason: I'll attach the pulley to the boom; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the pulley to be mounted on the boom, ready to guide a rope.

effect: The pulley is mounted at the boom tip; the spreading feet are the remaining offered combination.
reason: I'll add the feet to give the crane a wider, more stable base.
expectation: I expect the feet to help the crane resist tipping or wobbling.

effect: The spreading feet complete the braced crane frame, and Jo's nudge shows the triangles holding their shape.
reaction: The wider base is a satisfying finish, though the final fitting was straightforward.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the diagonal braces was most worthwhile: the rectangle-to-diamond explanation clearly showed why triangles resist sideways distortion.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequential boom and pulley fittings were rather repetitive, especially when only one combination was offered.

surprise.text: The fixed pulley changes the direction of the pull without halving the weight; that distinction was useful.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt arbitrary, although several fittings were selected mainly because they were the only offered combination.

continue.text: I would continue: the clear explanations of bracing and pulleys make me curious to see how the crane lifts the basket, despite the repetitive assembly steps.
